# OpsCat MCP server

Infrastructure ops for AI agents: read your events, cases, logs, synthetic checks,
incidents and monitored infrastructure straight from Claude Desktop, Claude Code,
Cursor or any MCP client.

Endpoint:  https://opscat.io/mcp   (Streamable HTTP, MCP revision 2025-11-25)

A self-hosted OpsCat serves the same endpoint on its own base URL.

## Connecting

Point your client at the endpoint above. It discovers the rest on its own:

- `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and
  `GET /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp` (RFC 9728) — both forms are
  served, so a client can bootstrap from our `WWW-Authenticate` challenge or by
  deriving the URL from the resource identifier.
- `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` (RFC 8414).
- `POST /oauth/register` (RFC 7591) — dynamic client registration. Public clients
  only: no `client_secret`, PKCE `S256` mandatory (`plain` is rejected).

Your browser opens the consent screen once. **If your account belongs to more than
one organization you pick which one this connection acts in** — the token is bound
to that organization and every tool is scoped to it. Connect a second organization
by running the flow again; your client then holds two connections.

Tokens: access 1 h, refresh 30 d with rotation (a reused refresh token is
rejected). Audience-bound per RFC 8707, so a token minted for another resource
cannot drive this one. Revoke with `POST /oauth/revoke`.

## Scopes

| Scope | Grants |
|---|---|
| `read` | Events, cases, logs, checks, incidents, infrastructure inventory, dashboard |
| `write` | Update cases, act on events, open/update incidents, schedule maintenance, run checks, poll vendors |

Your OpsCat role still applies on top: the scope says what the client asked for,
your membership role says what you may do. An `analyst` holding the `write` scope
still cannot perform `lead`-only actions — MCP mirrors the permissions the web app
enforces, never more and never less.

## Tools

Every tool is annotated (`readOnlyHint` / `destructiveHint` / `idempotentHint` /
`openWorldHint`) and returns `structuredContent` alongside its text block. A
read-only credential does not see the write tools at all — they are absent from
`tools/list`, not merely refused on call.

### Read (`read` scope)

- `opscat_get_dashboard` — one-call overview: active/critical events, open cases,
  failing checks, live incidents, active maintenance. **Start here.**
- `opscat_list_events` — deduplicated alerts. Filter by `status`
  (`active`/`finished`/`downgraded`/`all`), `minSeverity`, `limit`.
- `opscat_get_event` — one event with its last 20 log lines and linked case.
- `opscat_list_cases` — the unit of on-call work. Filter by `status`.
- `opscat_search_logs` — substring search over ingested logs. Narrow with
  `device` and `sinceMinutes` (default 60) — this can return a lot of text.
- `opscat_list_checks` — synthetic checks with their latest result;
  `onlyFailing: true` for the fast "what is down" read.
- `opscat_list_incidents` — incidents, including whether each is published to the
  public status page.
- `opscat_list_infrastructure` — agents, SNMP targets and heartbeats with
  last-seen times.
- `opscat_list_vendors` — third-party providers whose status pages OpsCat tracks;
  `onlyDisrupted: true` for the supply-chain problem list.

Severity is 0-100: >= 80 critical, >= 60 major, >= 40 minor.

### Write (`write` scope)

- `opscat_update_case` — status, root cause, note. The "acknowledge and write
  down what you found" tool.
- `opscat_event_action` — `finish` (also closes the case), `downgrade`, `note`.
- `opscat_create_incident` — opens an incident. Created **unpublished**: it is not
  on the public status page until you publish it.
- `opscat_post_incident_status` — move to `investigating`/`identified`/
  `monitoring`/`resolved` and append an update. On a published incident this text
  is **publicly visible**.
- `opscat_update_incident` — title, severity, RCA, and `published`. Publishing
  asks for confirmation first (see below).
- `opscat_create_maintenance` / `opscat_delete_maintenance` — maintenance windows
  suppress alerting. Deleting one is destructive and asks for confirmation.
- `opscat_run_checks` — run this org's synthetic checks now (`openWorldHint`: it
  contacts the external targets).
- `opscat_poll_vendor` — re-fetch one vendor's status feed now (`openWorldHint`).

**Confirmation.** Publishing an incident and deleting a maintenance window ask
the user through MCP elicitation. If your client does not support elicitation the
tool refuses and tells you to re-run with `confirm: true` — it never proceeds
silently.

**Roles apply on top of scopes.** The scope says what the client asked for; your
membership role says what you may do. Incidents and maintenance need `lead`;
cases, events, checks and vendor polls are available to `analyst` — exactly the
split the web app enforces.

## Resources

- `opscat://org/<id>/status` — the public status page payload, identical to what
  the page and its `.json` endpoint serve.
- `opscat://org/<id>/incidents/open` — unresolved incidents with their update
  history.

## Session lifecycle

Stateful. `initialize` returns an `mcp-session-id` header; send it on every
subsequent request. Only `initialize` opens a session — anything else that does
not resolve to a live one is answered `404` (`-32001`), so re-`initialize` and
carry on. Sessions are pruned after 1 h of inactivity, measured from the last
request, so an in-use session is never pruned out from under you. `DELETE /mcp`
with the session header closes cleanly.

The endpoint validates `Origin` and answers `403` for one that is not
allow-listed. Native clients send no `Origin` and are unaffected.

## Not exposed, deliberately

No tools for user management, API-key or credential management, organization or
billing administration, or super-admin functions. An agent that can mint
credentials is a privilege-escalation path with a natural-language interface.

## Driving OpsCat without MCP

The same operations API the web app uses accepts `Authorization: Bearer`, so a
script or a cron job needs no browser session and no MCP client:

    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://opscat.io/api/events
    curl -X PATCH -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
         -d '{"status":"closed"}' https://opscat.io/api/cases/42

Two credentials work there:

- an **MCP access token** (the one from the flow above) — acts as you, with your
  membership role, `read` scope for GET and `write` for anything else;
- an **API key with the `api` scope**, created under Settings -> API Keys — acts
  with the role assigned to the key, capped at the role of whoever created it.

No CSRF header is needed for Bearer requests (CSRF protects cookie auth). Account,
API-key, billing, organization and super-admin endpoints stay session-only: a
credential that can mint another credential would be a privilege-escalation path.

## Status page

The public status page needs no MCP client and no credential — append `.json` to
any status page URL:

    https://opscat.io/status.json
    https://opscat.io/status/<org-slug>.json

`https://opscat.io/summary.json` is the origin-level alias.
